body:
Update 2026-10-30: S009-02 and S009-04 are now started in their startable scope.

- S009-02 (internal scope): provider-fact mapping D1–D7 of the native 0.9/v5 candidate against the neutral requirements, plus compatibility/lifetime fixture inventory F-01–F-06 (defined, execution after a C139-02 candidate). Production adapter binding still waits for accepted C139-01.
- S009-04 (requirements scope): foundation needs N1–N8 roadmap with consume/supply map for core, freeze-blocker status and open questions for C139-01/REQ-140. Sign-off still waits for the agreed candidate, actual qualification and REQ-140 closure.

Both are documentation-only; no runtime behavior, API adoption or conformance is claimed. Documents: https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak.Schema/blob/feature/bounded-document-assessment/docs/S009-02-PROVIDER-FACT-MAPPING.md and .../docs/S009-04-FOUNDATION-REQUIREMENTS.md (uncommitted under the branch Git rule).

**2026-10-30 — S009-01 executed; S009-02 fixture inputs pinned** (branch `feature/bounded-document-assessment`, commit `c362499`).

- [S009-01 native coverage inventory](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak.Schema/blob/feature/bounded-document-assessment/docs/S009-01-NATIVE-COVERAGE-INVENTORY.md): inventory and demand-ranking complete. **No next implementation slice is selected** — no public/owner-authorized schema+instance fixture with expected typed-consumer operations is on record, and the Schema registration forbids adding grammar/coverage without a demonstrated use case. The exact owner ask is in §5: one public or owner-authorized schema + instance fixture with the expected typed-consumer operation. This unblocks slice selection; it is the intended outcome, not a gap.
- [S009-02 fixture identities](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak.Schema/blob/feature/bounded-document-assessment/docs/S009-02-FIXTURE-IDENTITIES.json): F-01..F-06 fixture inputs hash-pinned (commit + per-file sha256) against the 451-case suite source. Pinning is not execution evidence; execution still follows the accepted core contract.

Documentation only — no runtime behavior change, no grammar addition, no conformance claim. S009-02 production binding still waits for accepted core C139-01; S009-04 sign-off still waits for the agreed candidate, actual qualification and REQ-140 closure.

**2026-11-01 — R2 owner review packets registered (Schema side informed)**

The core repo now carries the prepared R2 owner review packets at `docs/foundation-r2-owner-review/README.md` (prepared 2026-11-01 against compiled draft `0890592e`; packet index `PACKETS.json` binds returns to the exact proposal manifest and decision-ledger hashes).

What this means for the Schema owner line:
- **Schema-owner returns are requested in two packets:** [O1](docs/foundation-r2-owner-review/O1.md) (with XmlDb: source-node membership, original node/facts association, snapshot-specific typed issuance) and [O2](docs/foundation-r2-owner-review/O2.md) (with Core: exact numeric/list/union contracts, N1–N8, advisor context, compatible-view supported/refused profiles).
- All seven role templates remain `NotSubmitted`; nothing is prefilled as accepted. Completeness check: `python -B docs/foundation-r2-owner-review/tools/returns.py --response <response.json>` (format/draft binding only).
- **S009-04 connection:** these packets are the executable path to the joint foundation sign-off recorded as pending in [S009-04-FOUNDATION-REQUIREMENTS](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak.Schema/blob/feature/bounded-document-assessment/docs/S009-04-FOUNDATION-REQUIREMENTS.md) — sign-off stays pending until the Schema returns for O1/O2 are actually submitted and reviewed. No acceptance is implied by this registration.
- Existing-return check: no matching explicit response found in the five searched local checkouts; remote issues/messages were not searched, so this is not proof no external answer exists.

Documentation/disposition step only — no production change, no engine suite rerun, no consumer-integration claim.

**Schema alignment needed for O1/O2 acceptance**

The packet questions need explicit Schema-owner dispositions, not just registration of the packets. Based on the audited capability boundary, the following would make the Schema returns reviewable and acceptance-ready. This is a proposed work/acceptance checklist, not a claim that the returns or runtime qualification are already complete.

### O1 — Source membership and original evidence (Schema + XmlDb)

1. **Map actual membership checks.** Against the pinned Schema and XmlDb source revisions, name the concrete provider methods/identities that implement `ISchemaAssessmentInput.OwnsNode` for each supported profile. Show the check uses actual source/snapshot membership before reading any getter on a purported foreign node, without materializing/copying the graph. Clearly mark any profile for which no such method is available as unsupported or a signature gap.
2. **Specify facts across copies and edits.** State exactly how node, facts, input, and origin remain associated. For preserve-copy, identify how the new snapshot’s node is bound to the original evidence; otherwise strip facts and require reassessment. Specify invalidation/reassessment after edits and rejection of independently compiled component handles, regardless of matching names/digests.
3. **Specify typed-value issuance order.** Confirm the operation requires the exact admitted snapshot, validates source membership and `OwnsTypedValue(value, input, originalAssessment)` before reading the container, then validates each atomic/type evidence. For ordinary XmlDb XML, assessor/origin remain absent—no fabricated Schema assessment. Fresh construction must not be represented as original PSVI.
4. **Attach cases or a pinned-source feasibility plan.** Cover same-source positive, foreign node rejected before getters, preserve/strip copy, stale edit, independently compiled component, and revoked input. Include the exact methods/files and any remaining infeasible/missing signature. Actual integration qualification can remain an R4 gate; do not imply it has run.

### O2 — Typed values, numeric policy and compatible views (Schema + Core)

1. **Disposition all six numeric member intents.** Confirm exact `BigInteger`/`XdmExactDecimal` representations and overload semantics; preserve wrong-kind checks and refuse overflow/inexact legacy narrowing rather than round. State how digit/scale/atom quotas apply before/during parsing and arithmetic as well as output/serialization, and identify the finite limits/default policy or explicitly record the unresolved decision. An already allocated `BigInteger` is not bounded retroactively.
2. **Close value-shape semantics.** Preserve list identity for empty and singleton lists, per-atomic selected union member/provenance, and the distinctions among nilled, no typed value, and empty typed list. Original PSVI remains original evidence; fresh construction supplies no original assessment. Enumerate backend-unsupported cases as explicit `Unsupported` without deleting required API shape.
3. **Disposition N1–N8, not only decimal.** State authority ownership/same-component rules; derivation, affiliation and complete-closure behavior; immutable captured host/query/XDM context and assessment episode; original node facts; lifetime/concurrency profile; and separation of source, snapshot, component authority and query environment. Return `Unsupported` when a complete supported answer is unavailable.
4. **Define directional compatibility.** Bind proof to exact source/target advisors and execution environment; preserve original facts/PSVI; return `Incompatible` only on a supported proof and `Unsupported` when proof is incomplete. QName/digest/label equality is not proof. List supported and refused profiles and any exact required signature gap. Signature disposition is not the positive runtime proof reserved for R4.

For each Schema return, provide answers to every Q, the exact source revision and supported/refused profile, decision, named signer/date, explicit unresolved-required-signature-gap list, and evidence references in the matching template. Keep `runtimeQualification`, C45 acceptance and API-freeze claims unset unless their separate gates are actually satisfied. O1/O2 are joint packets: Schema’s answers do not substitute for the XmlDb or Core co-owner returns, and the other owner’s signature should remain pending until independently supplied and reviewed.

**2026-11-02 — Schema BCAP-01 owner review status (O1/O2)**

I checked the Schema portion of `docs/foundation-bcap-owner-review/README.md` and the bound Schema templates against proposal manifest `ff475d712f6ef6aa5033113cc39afb887ae4cbad24705098c5c9cb2097641688`.

**Schema O1 and O2 are not accepted; both remain NotSubmitted.** The templates have no answers, decision, source revision, signer/date, profile, gap list, evidence, delta applicability, or original-exception-graph disposition. The previous Schema comment (#6563123351) is checklist guidance, not a formal return. The packet itself says Schema full returns remain required.

To make these returns reviewable, Schema must submit revised, manifest-bound forms that:
- answer every original O1/O2 question and map relevant BCAP R01–R08 delta applicability to the actual Schema profile, with exact source revision and evidence;
- for O1, disposition source membership, node/facts/input/origin association, preserve/strip and stale-edit behavior, typed-value issuance, and positive/foreign/copied/revoked cases or an explicit feasibility plan;
- for O2, disposition all six numeric intents and limits, list/union/PSVI semantics, N1–N8 authority/context/lifetime needs, and supported/refused directional compatibility; and
- explicitly address capture/error-graph implications, state any unresolved required signature gaps, and provide the owner’s decision, named signer and date.

Until those owner returns are submitted and reviewed, acceptance remains **Pending**. This is a design-review status only; it does not claim runtime qualification, C45 acceptance, API freeze, or product integration. I have not submitted or signed a return on behalf of the Schema owner.
